verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at any level. The patch changes comments only in nodeAppend.c, and Etsuro Fujita, who reviewed v1 in message #2, rewrote it as v2 and, per the brief, pushed it on 2026-11-10. Confidence is medium because the final v2 comment text and the commit are not in the material.

brief.title: Clarify wait versus poll in ExecAppendAsyncEventWait header comment
brief.problem: The header comment of ExecAppendAsyncEventWait in nodeAppend.c does not say when the function waits for events and when it only polls. This came up in review of another patch, and the reviewer, Etsuro Fujita, asked for the comment change as a separate patch. The audience is developers reading the async Append executor code.
brief.proposed_design: v1 adds to the header comment that the function waits when node->as_syncdone is true and polls without waiting otherwise. Etsuro Fujita's v2 rewrites that text using an existing in-function comment about timeout -1 versus 0. v2 then replaces that in-function comment with a brief one. The patch changes comments only.
author_claims: The header comment of ExecAppendAsyncEventWait can be improved.
The reviewer says v1 is not fully correct, because async execution still runs during polling when some events are ready.
The reviewer says the existing timeout comment is more accurate, and that v2 makes it redundant.
brief.thread_state: Etsuro Fujita reviewed v1, posted v2, and pushed it on 2026-11-10 after Chao Li agreed. The CommitFest entry still shows Needs review and Patch needs rebase, so its status has not caught up with the push.
unclear: The material does not show the final v2 comment text or its commit message.
The thread does not link the commit that Etsuro Fujita pushed, or say which branches got it.

committability.owner_note: Etsuro Fujita reviewed v1, wrote v2 in message #2, and pushed it per the brief. The owner needs to know the async Append executor code.
committability.liability: The accuracy of one header comment and one short in-function comment in nodeAppend.c. There is no runtime behaviour to own.
committability.author_follow_up: Chao Li replied the same day in message #3 and accepted v2. Nothing further is needed from the author.

priority.reason: The change helps developers who read the async Append code and costs nothing at run time. The brief says it was pushed on 2026-11-10, so the only remaining step is to update the CommitFest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extend comments on signal handling and cross-reference comments on signal handling functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: A comments-only patch expanded the signal handling section in miscadmin.h to cover ProcSignal and deferred signal handling during blocking calls. It also added cross-references between the main signal handling routines and that comment.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Mark Dilger pointed out that two new comments in interrupt.c contradict each other: one says normal user backends do not use its handlers, another says most backends use one of them. The author did not reply during two commitfests, so Daniel Gustafsson closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm closing this as Returned with Feedback as it there has been no response to
the review comment during two commitfests.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel Append implementation
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes Append parallel-aware, so workers spread across its subplans through a shared array under a spinlock. It also lets a partial Append include parallel-safe non-partial child paths, each run by at most one worker.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers raised design points, including whether worker distribution is worth its complexity next to allowing non-partial subpaths, keeping the partial-subplan bitmap out of the path, and costing when one worker scans a whole non-partial child. The author agreed to rework the patch but posted no new version, and the commitfest manager returned it because it had not been updated in two weeks.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There have been some reviews, but the patch has not been updated in
two weeks.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq should append error messages, not overwrite
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that libpq always append to conn->errorMessage during connection setup and query execution, instead of overwriting it, with only a few defined points that clear it. A second patch labeled each part of the error with the server and port being tried when several hosts are listed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because the thread had no activity after August and the patch set no longer applied cleanly. Before that, Robert Haas objected that reporting failures from every host adds noise: when the first host is down and the second rejects a password, the user only needs the password error. Tom Lane did not accept this, and the disagreement was not resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The last status of this patch comes from August, which has been
unanswered.  So I am marking the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make async slave to wait for lsn to be replayed
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a way for a hot standby session to wait until a given LSN has been replayed, with an optional timeout, so that reads on an async standby can see earlier writes. The interface changed several times: a standalone WAIT FOR command, then BEGIN ... WAIT FOR LSN, then BEGIN AFTER ... WITHIN, then pg_waitlsn functions, and finally a pg_waitlsn procedure.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They show that the interface was not settled after a commit in April 2020: later versions moved from BEGIN syntax to functions and then to a procedure, with Kyotaro Horiguchi asking how a procedure compares with a command. In March 2021 the patch failed to compile and was set to Waiting on Author, and no closing message is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improvements for pg_wal_replay_wait()
precedents_retrieved.summary: A follow-up patchset for the pg_wal_replay_wait() procedure, which waits on a standby until a given LSN is replayed. It rechecks the replay LSN after recovery ends, fixes comments and wording, adds tests for the error cases and stabilizes 043_wal_replay_wait.pl with wait_for_catchup() and pg_switch_wal().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown message, from September 2024, reports that the revised test passed 100 of 100 runs, and no objection to the patchset appears in the shown messages.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make Append Cost aware of some run time partition prune case
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner reduce the cost and row estimates of an Append path by estimating how many partitions survive run-time or init partition pruning, mainly for quals like partkey = $1. The goal is to make generic plans and join plans over partitioned tables be costed more accurately.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry stalled after the March 2021 patch no longer applied to master. vignesh C asked for a rebase in July 2021, the author did not post one, and Daniel Gustafsson returned it with feedback in November 2021. No design objection decided it, but the author's last patch left Parallel Append costing, MergeAppend and multiple partition keys unhandled.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As the thread has stalled, this patch still doesn't apply (judging by the log
it's likely not too hard to resolve).

precedents_retrieved.title: Adjust tuples estimate for appendrel
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets an appendrel's tuples estimate to the sum of the tuples of its live child relations instead of to its rows estimate. This lets estimate_num_groups() apply the formula from 84f9a35e3 to appendrels, which reduces the over-estimate of distinct groups that made the planner under-cost incremental sort.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Andrei Lepikhov supported committing the patch but asked for a regression test that checks the appendrel->tuples change directly, and the author had said he could not devise one. After that the discussion moved to wider ndistinct estimation ideas, and no later message from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: doc: Add some OID/TOAST-related limitations to the limits appendix.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a note to the limits appendix that a table can hold at most 4,294,967,296 out-of-line TOAST values, and that OID searches slow down inserts as the OID space fills. It also adds rows on the size and number of large objects in pg_largeobject.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why it was withdrawn. The last message is a second review from John Naylor that asks for more edits, and no author reply follows. He found the large object rows wrong (OIDs limit the number of large objects, not table size) and wanted the vacuum and partitioning advice removed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: We don't need to tell people to vacuum, and we don't need to tell them about partitioning as a workaround -- it's a workaround for the table size limit, too, but we are just documenting the limits here.

The patch changes one comment in nodeAppend.c and nothing user-facing. It adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour, pg_dump output or client-visible change, so the standards and compatibility angle has nothing to object to. A committer who knows the area reviewed it, rewrote it and pushed it.

The patch changes only comments in src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or ABI change, so there is nothing to object to from the replication and on-disk angle.
The patch changes only comments in nodeAppend.c. It adds no privileges, defaults, user-visible surface, or runtime behaviour, so there is nothing to object to on security grounds.

The patch changes comments in nodeAppend.c only. It adds no hot-path cost, no API, no dependency and no long-term commitment. The committer who reviewed it, Etsuro Fujita, knows the async Append code, rewrote it as v2 and pushed it (message #5). From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to.

The patch only changes comments in nodeAppend.c, and no extension or existing feature can stand in for a code comment. The angle also covers duplication: v2 removes the overlapping in-function comment, so the patch leaves less repeated text. The patch was pushed on 2026-11-10.

This is a comment-only change in nodeAppend.c, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. Readers of the async Append code gain, nobody pays, and the area committer asked for it, rewrote it, and pushed it in message #5.
